requirements.quote:
CONTINUATION frames do not result in state transitions; they are
   effectively part of the HEADERS or PUSH_PROMISE that they follow.
requirements.condition: When processing a CONTINUATION frame that follows a HEADERS or PUSH_PROMISE frame for stream-state purposes.
requirements.required_behavior: Treat the CONTINUATION frame as part of the HEADERS or PUSH_PROMISE frame it follows.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not cause a separate stream state transition for the CONTINUATION frame.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can process a HEADERS or PUSH_PROMISE sequence with CONTINUATION frames and verify that no transition is attributed independently to a CONTINUATION frame.

requirements.quote:
For the purpose of state transitions, the END_STREAM flag is
   processed as a separate event to the frame that bears it; a HEADERS
   frame with the END_STREAM flag set can cause two state transitions.
requirements.condition: When a received or sent frame bears the END_STREAM flag.
requirements.required_behavior: Process END_STREAM as a stream-state event separate from its containing frame, allowing a HEADERS frame with END_STREAM to cause two transitions.
requirements.why_checkable: State-transition instrumentation can verify separate processing of the frame event and END_STREAM event, including two transitions for HEADERS with END_STREAM.

requirements.quote: idle:  All streams start in the "idle" state.
requirements.condition: When a stream first exists in the endpoint's stream-state model.
requirements.required_behavior: Initialize the stream in the idle state.
requirements.why_checkable: The initial state of every modeled stream can be inspected before any state-changing event.

requirements.quote:
*  Sending a HEADERS frame as a client, or receiving a HEADERS
         frame as a server, causes the stream to become "open".  The
         stream identifier is selected as described in Section 5.1.1.
         The same HEADERS frame can also cause a stream to immediately
         become "half-closed".
requirements.condition: When a client sends HEADERS on an idle stream or a server receives HEADERS on an idle stream, without an additional condition that immediately half-closes it.
requirements.required_behavior: Transition the stream from idle to open.
requirements.why_checkable: A state-machine test can apply the role-specific HEADERS event to an idle stream and inspect the resulting open state.

requirements.quote:
*  Sending a HEADERS frame as a client, or receiving a HEADERS
         frame as a server, causes the stream to become "open".  The
         stream identifier is selected as described in Section 5.1.1.
         The same HEADERS frame can also cause a stream to immediately
         become "half-closed".
requirements.condition: When the HEADERS frame that opens an idle stream also carries the condition that closes the sending side, such as the separately processed END_STREAM event described in this chunk.
requirements.required_behavior: Permit the stream to transition immediately through open to the applicable half-closed state.
requirements.why_checkable: Combining this passage with the adjacent END_STREAM processing rule yields a concrete two-step transition that can be tested with HEADERS carrying END_STREAM.

requirements.quote:
*  Sending a PUSH_PROMISE frame on another stream reserves the
         idle stream that is identified for later use.  The stream state
         for the reserved stream transitions to "reserved (local)".
requirements.condition: When an endpoint sends a PUSH_PROMISE on another stream that identifies an idle promised stream.
requirements.required_behavior: Reserve the identified idle stream and transition it to reserved (local).
requirements.why_checkable: A test can send PUSH_PROMISE referencing an idle stream and inspect that promised stream's resulting state.

requirements.quote: Only a server may send PUSH_PROMISE frames.
requirements.condition: When an endpoint sends a PUSH_PROMISE frame.
requirements.required_behavior: The sending endpoint must have the server role.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: A client must not send PUSH_PROMISE frames.
requirements.why_checkable: The sender's role and emitted frame type are directly observable.

requirements.quote:
*  Receiving a PUSH_PROMISE frame on another stream reserves an
         idle stream that is identified for later use.  The stream state
         for the reserved stream transitions to "reserved (remote)".
requirements.condition: When an endpoint receives a PUSH_PROMISE on another stream that identifies an idle promised stream.
requirements.required_behavior: Reserve the identified idle stream and transition it to reserved (remote).
requirements.why_checkable: A test can deliver PUSH_PROMISE referencing an idle stream and inspect that promised stream's resulting state.

requirements.quote: Only a client may receive PUSH_PROMISE frames.
requirements.condition: When an endpoint receives a PUSH_PROMISE frame.
requirements.required_behavior: The receiving endpoint must have the client role.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: A server must not accept receipt of PUSH_PROMISE as a valid role-specific event.
requirements.why_checkable: The receiver's role and incoming frame type are directly observable.

requirements.quote:
*  Note that the PUSH_PROMISE frame is not sent on the idle stream
         but references the newly reserved stream in the Promised Stream
         ID field.
requirements.condition: When a PUSH_PROMISE reserves an idle stream.
requirements.required_behavior: Identify the newly reserved stream through the Promised Stream ID field while sending the PUSH_PROMISE on another stream.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not send the PUSH_PROMISE frame on the idle stream being reserved.
requirements.why_checkable: Frame placement and the Promised Stream ID field can be inspected and compared with the stream being reserved.

requirements.quote:
*  Opening a stream with a higher-valued stream identifier causes
         the stream to transition immediately to a "closed" state; note
         that this transition is not shown in the diagram.
requirements.condition: When opening a stream whose identifier is higher than that of another still-idle stream governed by this rule.
requirements.required_behavior: Transition the lower-valued idle stream immediately to closed.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can open a higher-numbered stream and inspect the state assigned to skipped lower-numbered streams.

requirements.quote:
Receiving any frame other than HEADERS or PRIORITY on a stream in
      this state MUST be treated as a connection error (Section 5.4.1)
      of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.condition: When any frame other than HEADERS or PRIORITY is received on an idle stream.
requirements.error_behavior: Treat the event as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can deliver each disallowed frame type on an idle stream and verify connection-level PROTOCOL_ERROR handling.

requirements.quote:
of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.  If this stream is initiated by the
      server, as described in Section 5.1.1, then receiving a HEADERS
      frame MUST also be treated as a connection error (Section 5.4.1)
      of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.condition: When a HEADERS frame is received on an idle stream that is server-initiated.
requirements.error_behavior: Treat the event as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can deliver HEADERS on an idle server-initiated stream and verify connection-level PROTOCOL_ERROR handling.

requirements.quote:
reserved (local):  A stream in the "reserved (local)" state is one
      that has been promised by sending a PUSH_PROMISE frame.
requirements.condition: When a stream has been promised by the local endpoint sending PUSH_PROMISE.
requirements.required_behavior: Represent the promised stream in the reserved (local) state.
requirements.why_checkable: The implementation's stream state can be inspected after locally sending a PUSH_PROMISE.

requirements.quote:
PUSH_PROMISE frame reserves an idle stream by associating the
      stream with an open stream that was initiated by the remote peer
      (see Section 8.4).
requirements.condition: When a PUSH_PROMISE reserves an idle stream.
requirements.required_behavior: Associate the reserved idle stream with an open stream initiated by the remote peer.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can inspect the promised stream, its associated parent stream, the parent's open state, and the parent's initiator.

requirements.quote:
*  The endpoint can send a HEADERS frame.  This causes the stream
         to open in a "half-closed (remote)" state.
requirements.condition: When the local endpoint sends HEADERS on a stream in reserved (local).
requirements.why_checkable: A state-machine test can send HEADERS from reserved (local) and inspect the resulting state.

requirements.quote:
*  Either endpoint can send a RST_STREAM frame to cause the stream
         to become "closed".  This releases the stream reservation.
requirements.condition: When either endpoint sends RST_STREAM for a stream in reserved (local).
requirements.required_behavior: Transition the stream to closed and release its reservation.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can send RST_STREAM from either side and verify both the closed state and reservation release.

requirements.quote:
An endpoint MUST NOT send any type of frame other than HEADERS,
      RST_STREAM, or PRIORITY in this state.
requirements.condition: When an endpoint sends a frame on a stream in reserved (local).
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not send any frame type other than HEADERS, RST_STREAM, or PRIORITY.
requirements.why_checkable: Outgoing frames on a reserved (local) stream can be inspected and checked against the three permitted types.

requirements.quote: A PRIORITY or WINDOW_UPDATE frame MAY be received in this state.
requirements.condition: When a PRIORITY or WINDOW_UPDATE frame is received on a stream in reserved (local).
requirements.required_behavior: Accept receipt of the frame as permitted in this state.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not reject the frame merely because the stream is in reserved (local).
requirements.why_checkable: A test can deliver each listed frame type in reserved (local) and verify it is not rejected solely due to stream state.

requirements.quote:
Receiving any type of frame other than RST_STREAM, PRIORITY, or
      WINDOW_UPDATE on a stream in this state MUST be treated as a
      connection error (Section 5.4.1) of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.condition: When a frame other than RST_STREAM, PRIORITY, or WINDOW_UPDATE is received on a stream in reserved (local).
requirements.error_behavior: Treat the event as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can deliver each disallowed frame type in reserved (local) and verify connection-level PROTOCOL_ERROR handling.

requirements.quote:
reserved (remote):  A stream in the "reserved (remote)" state has
      been reserved by a remote peer.
requirements.condition: When a stream has been reserved by the remote peer.
requirements.required_behavior: Represent the stream in the reserved (remote) state.
requirements.why_checkable: The implementation's stream state can be inspected after the remote peer reserves the stream.
